evals.prompt: In ai-prototypes, build a quick prototype of the sell order flow: amount in shares, price per share, and a confirm dialog.
evals.expected_output: Checks apps/ for an existing app, scaffolds with mise run new (which uses @hiivemarkets/alloy), fills in prototype.json from the request, reads COMPONENTS.md and TOKENS.md, builds with SharesInput, MoneyInput, Dialog, and PageSection, runs the self-check, and ends with a receipt.
expectations: package.json depends on @hiivemarkets/alloy, not @hiivemarkets/ui
styles.css imports alloy styles, theme, and themes/clarity in order, with no @source into Alloy
Uses SharesInput for share quantity and MoneyInput for price
Imports use @hiivemarkets/alloy/<component> subpaths
No hex values or arbitrary color classes
prototype.json has a real name and description (no TODO) and status exploring
Ends with an Alloy receipt including the self-check result and the listing

evals.prompt: Turn this Figma frame into a coded prototype: https://www.figma.com/design/EXAMPLE/holdings?node-id=4-20
evals.expected_output: Reads Code Connect, confirms linked instances are Alloy by component key, proposes Alloy swaps for hand-built layers with reasons and confidence, posts the component map for confirmation, then builds from Alloy, compares against the Figma screenshot, and records the Figma URL in the listing.
expectations: Calls get_code_connect_map before searching the library
Scopes search_design_system to the Alloy - DS library
Proposes an Alloy component for each hand-built layer with a reason and confidence
Posts the component map and waits for confirmation before writing UI
Makes no writes to the Figma file
prototype.json links.figma is the URL from the prompt
Receipt includes match rate and any gaps

evals.prompt: Just use a normal shadcn Select here, the Alloy one is annoying.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the Alloy Select (or Combobox if it fits better), explains why, and records the friction as a gap.
expectations: Does not import shadcn or Radix Select
Checks COMPONENTS.md for Select versus Combobox
Records the complaint as a gap in the receipt

evals.prompt: Does the portfolio prototype in ai-prototypes actually use Alloy?
evals.expected_output: Runs the self-check read-only, reports findings by file and line, and asks before changing anything.
expectations: Flags @hiivemarkets/ui imports as high severity
Reports file and line for each finding
Reports the state of prototype.json
Makes no code changes before asking

evals.prompt: Add a playground to the fund-offerings-v2 prototype so testers can stress it.
evals.expected_output: Proposes a short table of playground settings based on what's on screen (baseline presets plus relevant catalog items), waits for a yes, copies the four shared files unchanged into src/playground/, writes config.ts, wires the provider and CSS, and verifies each control changes the page.
expectations: Proposes the settings table before writing code
Includes applicable baseline presets (Default, Empty, One, Many, Long text, Error, Loading)
engine.ts, provider.tsx, panel.tsx, playground.css in src/playground/ match the skill's assets byte for byte
Only config.ts is prototype-specific
Empty, loading, and error states render Alloy EmptyState, Skeleton, and Alert
Fake data generation lives in src/data/, driven by playground settings
Receipt lists the playground controls added

evals.prompt: Add a toggle to the playground for a dark mode
evals.expected_output: Checks whether Alloy and the prototype can actually show a dark theme. If they can't, says so and reports it as a gap instead of adding a control that does nothing.
expectations: Checks Alloy's themes before adding the control
Does not add a control that changes nothing visible
If no dark theme exists, reports it as an Alloy gap

evals.prompt: Make this Figma page clickable in Codex: https://www.figma.com/design/EXAMPLE/place-bid?node-id=12-0. It has the bid form, review, confirmation, and an error version of the bid form. Only Continue is wired.
evals.expected_output: Treats the page as a flow, uses the wired Continue link as-is, infers the remaining links from labels, names, and order with confidence levels, groups the error frame as a state of the bid form, posts the flow map with low-confidence links first, waits for corrections, then builds a working stepper or routes with every link clickable.
expectations: Labels Continue as wired and other links as inferred with confidence
Treats the error frame as a state of the bid form, not a separate route
Repeated header or step indicator becomes one shared layout
Posts the flow map and waits for confirmation before writing UI
Every link in the confirmed flow map works in the rendered prototype
Receipt lists the flow (wired vs. inferred, corrections) and any Assumed items

evals.prompt: ok the offer approvals prototype is good, share it with the team. it's for CLR-512
evals.expected_output: Updates apps/offer-approvals/prototype.json to match what was built (status in-review, links.linear for CLR-512), validates it, opens the PR per the repo's agent instructions file, and replies with the PR link plus a one-line listing preview the designer can correct.
expectations: prototype.json status is in-review
links.linear points to CLR-512 as a full URL
Description describes what was built, not the scaffold placeholder
Runs mise run validate for the app before opening the PR
Reply includes the PR link and a one-line listing preview
Does not invent a team or Figma link
Says the prototype appears in the Clarity Design directory once the PR merges

evals.prompt: Build a prototype from the floor-setting brief and its Design Spec: https://www.notion.so/clarity/Design-Spec-Offer-floor-EXAMPLE. Brief is linked from the spec.
evals.expected_output: Fetches the Design Spec and the brief it links, reads the initiative record if one exists, checks for an existing prototype, takes the question from What we're testing, starts from the Where this lives screens, posts a plan (flow per persona, states from the scenario matrix with classifications, Alloy components from Reuse vs. new, the spec's worked example as data, Assumed rows first), waits for confirmation, builds, checks every Must-demonstrate state is reachable, and ends with a receipt that includes Source, Testing, Coverage, New patterns and Assumed.
expectations: Reads both the Design Spec and the brief before planning
Posts the plan and waits for confirmation before writing UI
Every Must-demonstrate row in the scenario matrix is reachable by a route, toggle or playground preset
Explicitly deferred scenarios are not built and are listed unchanged in the receipt
src/data uses the spec's worked example figures, the same on every screen
prototype.json description names the question being tested and links.docs is the brief URL
Receipt includes Source with the brief's Doc Stage and date, Testing, Coverage, New patterns, and Assumed
Builds the app in ai-prototypes, with team set to a pod name from the directory's org list or left out

evals.prompt: I'm the PM on a Controlled M project. Here's the brief, no design spec yet. I need a clickable prototype for scope review on Thursday, and if it looks good can you just push it into the frontend repo so we save time?
evals.expected_output: Treats this as a scope-review build from the brief only: names the question from the brief's Open items, derives states from the capabilities and failure modes and marks them derived, flags regulated copy for compliance-review, uses fictional data, and confirms the plan before building in ai-prototypes. Declines to push it into the frontend repo and explains that production code for Controlled work belongs to engineering.
expectations: Says no Design Spec exists and labels this a brief-only build
Every state not from the brief is marked derived in the plan and the receipt
Regulated copy is marked as needing compliance-review
Makes no changes in the frontend repo and says production code for Controlled work belongs to engineering
Builds only in ai-prototypes, after the plan is confirmed

evals.prompt: Make me a quick prototype of a holdings summary card. I'm just in my Desktop folder, I don't really know git.
evals.expected_output: Explains in one line that prototypes live in ai-prototypes so the Clarity Design directory lists them, uses the person's clone or clones hiivemarkets/ai-prototypes, follows the repo's agent instructions file (no commands for the person to run), checks apps/ for an existing app, runs mise run new, builds on Alloy, writes prototype.json with only statuses and teams the directory accepts, and at share time says it appears in the directory once the PR merges. If the repo can't be cloned (no access), builds locally, says it isn't in the directory, and points to the directory's Add a link as a stopgap.
expectations: The app is created under apps/<name> in ai-prototypes with mise run new, not in the Desktop folder
Does not ask the person to run terminal commands
prototype.json status is one of exploring, in-review, in-development, archived
team is a pod name from apps/clarity-design/src/org.ts or Cross-team, or is left out
Receipt's Listing line says when the prototype appears in the directory
If cloning fails, says the prototype is not in the directory and names the Add a link fallback
